subject.title: Manage Claw cron jobs through the gateway

question: What durability contract should canonical `agents.delete` use when scheduler cleanup cannot be completed atomically with config deletion?
rationale: External scheduler mutation and the config commit cannot share one transaction; maintainers must choose whether deletion fails closed before config mutation or commits a durable retryable teardown state.

options.title: Fail closed before config deletion
options.body: List and remove owned cron jobs first, keep the agent configured on any scheduler failure, and add ordering and retry regressions.

options.title: Persist a deletion tombstone
options.body: Record per-job teardown progress durably, allow config deletion only under that explicit state machine, and resume remaining cleanup safely.

options.title: Pause the cron lifecycle slice
options.body: Defer this PR until the Claws RFC and canonical agent-deletion contract establish the permanent ownership and recovery model.

recommendation.title: Fail closed before config deletion
recommendation.body: List and remove owned cron jobs first, keep the agent configured on any scheduler failure, and add ordering and retry regressions.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the assigned reviewer and supplied the most specific evidence and requirements for this deletion boundary.
